title: Western Blotting Protocol
author: Karina L Conkrite
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6rmhd46
materials: Lyse cells on ice for 15-30 minutes.

To make 1L of 1X TG Running buffer: Component Volume end conc 10X Tris-Glycine buffer, BioRad 1610771 100 mL 1X 20% SDS, Technova S0293 5 mL 1% H2O 895mL 10X Tris-Glycine buffer Bio-Rad Laboratories Catalog #1610771 This buffer may be stored at 4 °C for a time. If using the Criterion set up, buffer may be reused in the tank, but should be fresh in the loading chamber. If using the SureLock boxes, you will use the entire liter every time. Also, prep for the transfer. This is very dependent on the size of your proteins of interest. If you are interested in proteins over 150 kDa, you will want to perform a fully wet transfer, possibly overnight in the cold room. In that case, for TG gels, you need to prep the buffer for the transfer, cut the membrane (1) and 3M filter papers (4) necessary to sandwich the transfer. Immobilon-P PVDF Membrane, 0.45um, roll Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #IPVH00010 Whatman Grade 3MM Chr Cellulose Western Blotting Membranes, GE Healthcare, Grade 3MM Chr Blotting Paper, roll, 10 cm × 100 m, VWR International (Avantor) Catalog #21427-546

Develop the blot, using the ECL detection method of choice. Lowly expressed proteins, recommend SuperSignal™ West Femto Maximum Sensitivity Substrate Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #34095 for other, more abundant proteins, less sensitive substrates may be used. carefully, without touching anything other than the edges of the blot, remove from TBST and place in a sheet protector. Try to remove all extra TBST. Apply ECL substrate uniformly to the blot with a pipet, then close the top half of the sheet protector to allow even distribution of the chemical.

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh lysis buffer daily and store on ice during use.

substeps.instruction: Combine the following per 1 mL 1X buffer: 200 uL 5X stock, 100 uL 10% Triton X-100, 10 uL 0.1M DTT, 10 uL 100X Protease/Phosphatase Inhibitor (Cell Signaling, Cat #5872), and 680 uL ddH2O.
Ensure final concentrations are 1 mM DTT, 1% Triton X-100, and 1X Protease/Phosphatase Inhibitor.

steps.title: Treat and Collect Cells
steps.instruction: Grow cells in culture and treat with desired chemicals, drugs, siRNA, or plasmids.

substeps.instruction: Collect protein generally 72 hours post-treatment (or 48-96 hours depending on cell cycle/protein cycling).
Remove media and wash cells with DPBS.
Collect cells as a pellet for later lysis or lyse directly using 100X Protease/Phosphatase Inhibitor (Cell Signaling, Cat #5872).

steps.title: Lyse and Clarify Protein
steps.instruction: Break membranes and isolate the protein supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Sonicate with a probe sonicator (Brodeur Lab, setting 6) for 5 seconds.
Centrifuge at 15000g or more for 15 minutes at 4 °C.
Transfer supernatant to a clean tube, avoiding the pellet.
Store at -80 °C if necessary, avoiding freeze/thaw cycles and aliquoting if needed.

steps.title: Quantify Protein Concentration
steps.instruction: Perform a BCA assay to determine protein levels for gel loading.

substeps.instruction: Use the Pierce BCA Protein Assay Kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Cat #23225).
Ensure samples fall within the standard curve; if not, redo the assay with different sample:lysis buffer dilutions.

steps.title: Prepare Protein Samples for Loading
steps.instruction: Prepare samples on ice (0 °C) with loading buffer.

substeps.instruction: Select the appropriate Tris-Glycine gel percentage based on the protein of interest.
Determine the amount of protein to load (e.g., 15ug or 30ug).
Aliquot the protein and add 2X SDS Gel Loading Buffer (Laemmli Buffer, stored at -20 °C) and lysis buffer to reach a standard volume for all samples.
Prepare ladders according to their specific boiling instructions.

2X SDS Gel Loading Buffer composition (for 4mL): 1 mL 0.5 M Tris-HCl pH 6.8 (125 mM final), 0.8 mL Glycerol (20% final), 0.8 mL 20% SDS (5% final), 0.4 mL 10% b-Mercaptoethanol (10% final), 0.2 mL 0.5% Bromophenol Blue (0.025% final), and 0.8 mL H2O.

steps.title: Prepare Gel and Running Buffer
steps.instruction: Set up the electrophoresis apparatus and buffers.

substeps.instruction: Prepare necessary buffers (e.g., ~1L TG running buffer for 2 Tris-Glycine gels).
Remove plastic barriers from the bottom of pre-cast gels.
Assemble the gel/box cartridge with the higher gel casing on the outside of the box.
Fill buffer chambers with running buffer.
Carefully remove combs and flush the wells with running buffer using a p200 or p1000 pipette.

steps.title: Denature and Load Samples
steps.instruction: Heat samples and load them into the gel.

substeps.instruction: Boil samples for TG gels at 95 °C for 10 minutes using lid locks.
Briefly spin down tubes to collect samples.
Load samples into the gel using gel loading tips or Rainin p20 tips.

steps.title: Run the Gel
steps.instruction: Electrophorese the proteins through the gel.

substeps.instruction: For TG gels, start at 75V for ~20 minutes to pass through the stacking gel.
Increase voltage according to gel type/percentage (refer to Novex/Criterion TGX info sheets).
Run samples to the bottom of the gel.

steps.title: Transfer Proteins to Membrane
steps.instruction: Transfer proteins from the gel to a membrane using the appropriate method.

substeps.instruction: For low to medium molecular weight (20-150 kDa), use the TransBlot Turbo system.
For higher molecular weight proteins, use a traditional wet transfer (recommended overnight in the cold room).
Ensure buffers are cold and check the current during transfer.

steps.title: Verify Transfer Efficiency
steps.instruction: Optional: Check transfer success using Ponceau stain.

substeps.instruction: Stain with 0.1% Ponceau S in 7% trichloroacetic acid (TCA) for 5 minutes.
Rinse in deionized water (transient staining) or 10% acetic acid (permanent staining) and air dry.
If blotting immediately, do not let the membrane dry; apply blocking solution or place in TBST.

steps.title: Block the Membrane
steps.instruction: Block the membrane to reduce non-specific antibody binding.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 5% milk in TBST: add 5g powdered milk to 50 mL TBST, shake, add remaining 50 mL TBST, and mix on a stir plate until uniform.
Block the membrane in 5% milk in TBST for 1 hour with rocking (8 mL is sufficient for one 9X10cm mini gel in Perfect Western boxes).

steps.title: Section Membrane and Apply Primary Antibody
steps.instruction: Optionally cut the membrane and incubate with the primary antibody.

substeps.instruction: If splitting the membrane, use a clean scalpel and ruler while the membrane is in a sheet protector.
Mix antibody to the specified concentration in blocking milk (or PBS with serum). Example: for 1:2500 beta-Actin, mix 8 mL milk with 3.2 uL antibody.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C with rocking.

steps.title: Wash and Apply Secondary Antibody
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane and incubate with an HRP-conjugated secondary antibody.

substeps.instruction: Remove blot from 4 °C, rinse quickly in TBST, and wash 3 x 10 minutes in TBST with rocking.
Dilute HRP-conjugated secondary antibody (matching the primary host species) in 5% milk in TBST (e.g., Anti-Mouse IgG Goat Polyclonal, Cat #115-035-003 at 1:25000).
Apply and incubate with rocking for 1 hour.

steps.title: Final Wash and Imaging
steps.instruction: Perform final washes and capture images of the blot.

substeps.instruction: Discard secondary antibody, rinse quickly in TBST, and wash 3 x 10 minutes in TBST with rocking.
Expose the blot using the Fluor-Chem Q in CTRB 3300.
Ensure focus is correct and the iris is open as far as possible to optimize images without overexposing.

steps.title: Strip and Re-probe Blot
steps.instruction: Optional: Remove antibodies to probe for different targets.

substeps.instruction: Place blot protein-side facing inside a hybridization tube.
Apply 10 mL Restore™ Western Blot Stripping Buffer (Cat #21059).
Incubate in the hyb oven at 37 °C for 15-20 minutes while turning.
Place blot back in TBST, rinse quickly, and wash 3 x 10 minutes in TBST.
Repeat from the Blocking step.
